title: Contains Duplicate
statement: Given an integer array `nums`, return `True` if any value appears **at least twice**, and `False` if every element is different.

example.why: The value 1 appears at index 0 and again at index 3.

idea: Comparing every number with every other number works, but that is O(n²) comparisons.
What we really need is a fast way to ask *have I seen this number before?*
A **hash set** answers that in O(1). Walk the list once: if the current number is already in the set it is a duplicate; otherwise add it and move on.

complexity.timeWhy: One pass; each set lookup and insert takes O(1) on average.
complexity.spaceWhy: If all numbers are different, the set ends up holding every one of them.

steps.text: Our example: **`nums = [1,2,3,1]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
Start with an empty **hash set**. It will hold every number we have already walked past.
Is 1 already in the set? No — this is the first time we see 1.
Add 1 to the set, so a later copy of it will be recognised instantly.
Is 2 already in the set? No — this is the first time we see 2.
Add 2 to the set, so a later copy of it will be recognised instantly.
Is 3 already in the set? No — this is the first time we see 3.
Add 3 to the set, so a later copy of it will be recognised instantly.
Is 1 already in the set? **Yes** — we have met 1 before, so the list has a duplicate.
Return **True** straight away. There is no need to look at the rest of the list.
Done — the answer is **`True`**. The value 1 appears at index 0 and again at index 3.
